Tender fraud in the City of Cape Town

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
It's a story of death threats, kidnapping and tender fraud within the City of Cape Town's housing Departmnet

Unique Selling Point:
This story sounds like plot from soapy. Muslim brother in laws in the construction industry in Cape Town fight it out for lucrative City of Cape Town Tenders. Raziek Rajah exposes his brother in laws Asif Khan corruption and the consequences: Death threats, kidnapping of his father, bribes, and the bankrupting of his successful construction company.

The directors of TCC and 2 COCT officials have been arrested and charged with fraud over a construction projects- the trail comes to court on the 12th March. But we have documents relating to inflated scaffolding costs which do not form part of the trial and be fresh evidence which the rest of the press do not have

Summary:
In 2020 Good Hope Construction GHC was awarded a tender by the City of Cape Town to fix stairways on the city council Flats which had deteriorated badly, and people had fallen and been badly injured. The tender was for R26 Million odd rand. GHC was in the process of finalising the paperwork with the City when the contract got stalled for a bunch of technical reasons and GHC began to investigate. Then Mayor Dan Plato instigated an investigation and there is a report that says R300 million was spent irregularly but the City has refused to release this report. During the investigation the head of City Safety and Security Investigation Unit Reynold Talamakies approached GHC director and offered him R30 million rand by TCC to drop the investigation against the City and TCC. Raziek has this recording. Talamakies has subsequently been arrested and will turn State Witness.
TCC Construction was awarded a tender by the City of Cape Town made up of 49 different projects and over charged for scaffolding. For example TCC would charge R800 000 million and a comparative quote for the same scaffolding for the same period of time was R18 600. TCC construction were not only paid excessively for scaffolding but it should normally be included as part of any job, but TCC charged for it over and above. These invoices were approved by a City official Alistar Standbul who has subsequently been arrested. We have the paper trail to prove this.
Good Hope Construction have a letter from the city manager where they agreed their tender was terminated irregularly but states that it needs to be fought out in court, GHC cannot afford the court case, and the stairways have yet to be repaired.

In that period R26 million that should have been spent rebuilding the stairways has been spent by TCC on various inflated and irregular building projects. When the City is pressed to release the report that reveals R300 million was irregularly spent the City say they are investigating, and have not released the report.


Further information:
Storyline- we start on the stairways on the Cape Flats with Fadiel Adams from the Cape Coloured Party and local residents who have been injured. The City awarded a tender of R26 million rand to repair the stairs- but 3 years later they look - what went wrong?
Raziek Rajah of GHC was ready to get working and was finalising the paperwork- people were hired it was a matter of weeks before they began the 3-year project
Crime fighter Hanif Loonat gets a tip off about same shady construction deals and visits his friend Raziek to understand how the City construction contracts works-. The company in question is TCC- owned by Raziek brother-in-law, and Raziek life begins to unravel
The Good Hope contract with the City is stalled by technicalities- Raziek is visited by the head of the SIU who offers him 30 million rand from TCC to stop digging – he refuses and in his investigations discovers that his brother in law is over charging for scaffolding - he has the evidence. Co-incidentally the same amount of R26 million is spent on TCC construction that would have been spent on repairing the stairs awarded the GHC.
Raziek father is kidnapped- Raziek gets death threats- GHC goes into liquidation.
The City of Cape Town have a report in 2021 which exposes R300 million is irregularly spent but they refuse to release it to the public, and say they investigating.
8 people are arrested on fraud charges, including 2 City officials. The City say they have changed their procurement system, the officials in question have resigned, But how have they just been awarded a clean audit when this tills hangs in the air?

Masa “ Tell me what happened when you fell ”
Kathleen “ I came out of my house and the step was loose and I tumbled right down and fell here
Masa ” What injuries did you have?”
Kathleen “My head, my eye, my back
Masa” Are you afraid you might have another accident”
Kathleen ” Yes, maybe I am dead that time”
Script: Her back still aches.
Kathleen “You go to the council, but the council never comes out
Script: Community activist Desmond Syce, points out another stairway - and says across Manneberg- there are plenty more
Desmond Syce “ and elderly women she actually fell through the backside and broke her hip. This is our reality this is how we live, most of our people are unemployed, we can’t even better this for ourselves, this is how it is in Manenberg.
Script: The company awarded the contract to replace these stairs - was Good Hope Construction
Raziek: The contract entailed two facets, one being an emergency replacement of staircases that were imminent to fall ……And then the other part was replacement of staircases that were ailing structures over the last 30 to 40 years.
Script: Raziek Rajah had just successfully replaced over 400 staircases for the City

Upsound Rajah “Well basically you had an existing aling staircase that was demolished and removed

Script: So when they were awarded the new contract - they sent out notices to Manenberg residents - that they were on the way.

But after four months, work had not begun. Local councillor Fadiel Adams- suspected corruption was at play, involving 10’s of millions of rand?

Fadiel: the city is hiding a lot about 300 million of fraud on the staircases only, we have got other things we are probing

Script: Adams accused Rajah of stealing the money. So Rajah put pressure on the City to release the funds - to his horror - he discovered the City had cancelled the contract - because of a technical flaw in the advertising of the tender.

Masa: is there a possibility that it was awarded irregularly?

Raziek: If there was, then there should have been an explanation. You cannot have a tender go through bid evaluation, bid adjudication, final assessment, final negotiation by city, we receive an award letter. And then you say to me that something irregular was done.

Masa: was money allocated for the first year? Was there a budget for this?

Raziek: We received the evidence confirming that there was a budget allocated. It was duly signed off…00:05:48:14 .and what it done was we were hit with COVID, had it been normal trading circumstances, we would have probably been able to pick up other contracts.

Script: Things went from bad to worse- Good Hope Construction went into liquidation - and 550 people lost their jobs.
Uncannily - around the same time community crime fighter Hanif Loonat - was alerted to another tender problem within the Cities housing Department - involving a company -called The Construction Company - TCC
Hanif: I was approached sometime in early 2020….by a subcontractor who worked very closely with TCC and was extremely disgruntled because he wasn't given the expected job….he decided to expose something that he was suspicious of
Script: Loonat wanted technical advice from Rajah on the Cities tender processes.

Hanif: When I approached him, he told me he doesn't want to get involved, because it's family.

Script: Turns out - The Construction Company – TCC- that Loonat was investigating is owned by Asif Khan - Rajah’s brother-in-law. This is where things got VERY messy- unleashing - the most acrimonious family feud.
Had corrupt City officials channelled the money from Rajah’s cancelled contract - to his brother in law company. Money they could allegedly siphon from dodgy maintenance contracts.
Raziek We had a contract awarded to us if it was irregularly, illegally or dubiously cancelled, I wanted to understand where was the budget of our contract move to what went on
Script: Were corrupt City officials in cahoots with TCC?
Hanif “ I worked endlessly in trying to get the mayor, the city manager to the party. I was fortunate that the ex-mayor Dan Plato, he instituted an inquiry.

Script: The Cities investigation into the housing maintenance department - allegedly uncovered 300 million rands of irregular spending - implicating TCC and others.

Hanif: “Initially I was approached by one of the senior city of Cape Town staff offering me a bribe to accept for our pain and suffering as a result of this tender being illegally cancelled.

Script: Rajah wanted nothing to do with the 30 million rand bribe - allegedly offered by Asif Khan of TCC. He dismissed the allegation in an online interview while on bail.

Asif:. I don't know. I've never knew him up until this investigation, even if he did make a bribe why would I use a stranger to do it when we've had three family mediations?

Script: The family had tried to resolve the conflict
Masa:. Is this not just a family feud?
Raziek: It's got nothing to do with the family feud. I am complaining about the city of Cape Town illegally cancelling my contract. How is that rationalized into a family feud?

Script: Why would the City and the Hawks undertake a three year investigation - if this was just a family spat? Community crime fighter Loonat - laid criminal charges - and the directors of TCC along with two City of Cape Town officials - were arrested for fraud.
Upsound
One of the allegations is TCC forged quotations to inflate the price of scaffolding. We found the allegedly forged quotations. The first company was called Scafhire – all the addresses listed were a dead end - and the phone just rings.
Asif: forensic audit was released and we listened to some of the allegations that came about. I have heard that this company may have closed down,

Script: Next up was Nexus Scaffolding - they pointed out they had dealt with TCC directly but only 4 months after TCC -had allegedly forged their quotes. We compared their actual quote with the earlier one that was allegedly falsified: Same specs, but more than R250 thousand rand difference." ?
Asif ” I'm not sure what the problem is and where this allegation stems from, because even though we may submit quotes and let's assume that a quote was fabricated, it still goes through a process They have to go through the codes, they have to test the rates and see that it's actually fair market value that the client is going to be getting for paying that.
Script: In court later that month Nexus Scaffolding added fuel to the fire- not only had TCC allegedly falsified two of their quotations - but also tried to involve them in a shady deal. The charge sheet read
“TCC offered to pay them upfront, more than the quoted amount, and Nexus should refund the difference after the job was done……Nexus declined their offer.
Script: Fighting back has cost the Rajah family enormously -

Raziek ”The onslaught became heavy It became heavy to an extent of death threats and the list goes on

Script: Then, in what had already been a saga of dramatic twists, Rajah's father Ismail was kidnapped from outside the office. Fingers were immediately pointed at TCC

Asif “How is someone going to prove something out of thin air- there is no such thing, there never will be such evidence. He states that one of his captors mentions my name Asif Khan it beats me why a captor who is kidnapping a person want to mention my name.

Script: Could all this have been avoided if the City of Cape Town had been more transparent - about the forensic report?

LINK The City of Cape Town sat on this forensic report, for two and half years which corroborated the NPAs case against its two officials and TCC and yet the City still claim there is no fraud or corruption within their housing Department
Script: They sent this reply to our questions and denied access to the forensic report.
“The City has a zero tolerance to corruption. It has been supporting the SAPS in their investigation
Script: Rajah, Adams, Loonat and the community continue to be stonewalled
Fadiel “How hard can it be for me as an elected councillor to ask for an expenditure report? We want to know where this money went and be told, No, we can't give it to you. The mayor is adamant that there's no evidence of crime in the report.
Script: Somethings up - The director of Housing Maintenance Department has been fired. City official Alistair Stanbul involved with both Good Hope Constructions and TCC contracts - is on trial - alongside TCC.
Raziek “ when you raise fraud and corruption in South Africa, you are vilified. Something needs to stop. You cannot have functional businesses be destroyed

Script: And stairways across the Cape Flats continue to crumble - will the court case provide answers?

City official Alistair Stanbul involved with both Good Hope Constructions and TCC contracts - is on trial - alongside TCC. Raziek “ when you raise fraud and corruption in South Africa, you are vilified. Something needs to stop. You cannot have functional businesses be destroyed Script: And stairways across the Cape Flats continue to crumble - will the court case provide answers?

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): It's a story of death threats, kidnapping and tender fraud within the City of Cape Town's housing Departmnet
metadata.Unique Selling Point: This story sounds like plot from soapy. Muslim brother in laws in the construction industry in Cape Town fight it out for lucrative City of Cape Town Tenders. Raziek Rajah exposes his brother in laws Asif Khan corruption and the consequences: Death threats, kidnapping of his father, bribes, and the bankrupting of his successful construction company. The directors of TCC and 2 COCT officials have been arrested and charged with fraud over a construction projects- the trail comes to court on the 12th March. But we have documents relating to inflated scaffolding costs which do not form part of the trial and be fresh evidence which the rest of the press do not have
metadata.Summary: In 2020 Good Hope Construction GHC was awarded a tender by the City of Cape Town to fix stairways on the city council Flats which had deteriorated badly, and people had fallen and been badly injured. The tender was for R26 Million odd rand. GHC was in the process of finalising the paperwork with the City when the contract got stalled for a bunch of technical reasons and GHC began to investigate. Then Mayor Dan Plato instigated an investigation and there is a report that says R300 million was spent irregularly but the City has refused to release this report. During the investigation the head of City Safety and Security Investigation Unit Reynold Talamakies approached GHC director and offered him R30 million rand by TCC to drop the investigation against the City and TCC. Raziek has this recording. Talamakies has subsequently been arrested and will turn State Witness. TCC Construction was awarded a tender by the City of Cape Town made up of 49 different projects and over charged for scaffolding. For example TCC would charge R800 000 million and a comparative quote for the same scaffolding for the same period of time was R18 600. TCC construction were not only paid excessively for scaffolding but it should normally be included as part of any job, but TCC charged for it over and above. These invoices were approved by a City official Alistar Standbul who has subsequently been arrested. We have the paper trail to prove this. Good Hope Construction have a letter from the city manager where they agreed their tender was terminated irregularly but states that it needs to be fought out in court, GHC cannot afford the court case, and the stairways have yet to be repaired. In that period R26 million that should have been spent rebuilding the stairways has been spent by TCC on various inflated and irregular building projects. When the City is pressed to release the report that reveals R300 million was irregularly spent the City say they are investigating, and have not released the report.
metadata.Further information: Storyline- we start on the stairways on the Cape Flats with Fadiel Adams from the Cape Coloured Party and local residents who have been injured. The City awarded a tender of R26 million rand to repair the stairs- but 3 years later they look - what went wrong? Raziek Rajah of GHC was ready to get working and was finalising the paperwork- people were hired it was a matter of weeks before they began the 3-year project Crime fighter Hanif Loonat gets a tip off about same shady construction deals and visits his friend Raziek to understand how the City construction contracts works-. The company in question is TCC- owned by Raziek brother-in-law, and Raziek life begins to unravel The Good Hope contract with the City is stalled by technicalities- Raziek is visited by the head of the SIU who offers him 30 million rand from TCC to stop digging – he refuses and in his investigations discovers that his brother in law is over charging for scaffolding - he has the evidence. Co-incidentally the same amount of R26 million is spent on TCC construction that would have been spent on repairing the stairs awarded the GHC. Raziek father is kidnapped- Raziek gets death threats- GHC goes into liquidation. The City of Cape Town have a report in 2021 which exposes R300 million is irregularly spent but they refuse to release it to the public, and say they investigating. 8 people are arrested on fraud charges, including 2 City officials. The City say they have changed their procurement system, the officials in question have resigned, But how have they just been awarded a clean audit when this tills hangs in the air?
